title: An Improved Two‐Step Collagenase Perfusion Protocol for Isolation of Mouse Primary Hepatocytes
markdown:
## Protocol: Protocol for isolation and short-term culture of primary mouse hepatocytes using two-step collagenase perfusion

### Overview

This protocol details the isolation and short-term culture of primary mouse hepatocytes via a two-step collagenase perfusion method. The process involves preparing specific perfusion solutions, surgically exposing the liver, performing sequential in situ perfusions with calcium-free and calcium-containing collagenase solutions, harvesting the tissue, mechanically dissociating the cells, and purifying them through filtration and centrifugation.

### Materials/Reagents

- Perfusion Solution I: HBSS (1 X), 50 mM EGTA, 1.0 M glucose, Penicillin-streptomycin.
- Perfusion Solution II: HBSS (1 X), 1.0 M CaCl2, 1.0 M glucose, Penicillin-streptomycin, Collagenase Type II or IV.
- Wash Medium: DMEM with Penicillin-streptomycin.
- Culture Coating: 0.01% rat-tail collagen solution.
- Serum-free DMEM for mechanical dissociation.
- PBS for washing coated plates.

### Equipment

- Isoflurane anesthesia system.
- Surgical instruments (scalpel, forceps).
- 70% Ethanol spray.
- Perfusion pump (e.g., LINA-9A).
- Cannula/Needle (0.45*15 mm).
- Wet cotton-tipped swabs.
- Petri dishes.
- Sterile filter or sterile gauze.
- Sterile 50 mL conical tubes.
- Centrifuge capable of 4°C operation.
- Sterile hood.

### Safety & Sterility

Maintain strict aseptic technique throughout the procedure. After surgical exposure, all subsequent steps involving cell handling must be performed in a sterile hood. Instruments and the mouse should be sprayed with 70% ethanol prior to surgery. Ensure no air bubbles enter the perfusion line during both perfusion steps to prevent liver damage and cell death.

## Reagent Preparation

### Preparation

1. Prepare Perfusion Solution I (50 mL per mouse) by mixing 48.725 mL of HBSS (1 X), 500 μL of 50 mM EGTA (for calcium chelation), 275 μL of 1.0 M glucose, and 500 μL of Penicillin-streptomycin. Prewarm this solution for at least 15 minutes at 37°C before use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare Perfusion Solution II (40 mL per mouse) by mixing 39.32 mL of HBSS (1 X), 60 μL of 1.0 M CaCl2, 220 μL of 1.0 M glucose, 400 μL of Penicillin-streptomycin, and 10 mg of Collagenase (Type II or IV). Prewarm this solution for at least 15 minutes at 37°C before use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare DMEM supplemented only with Penicillin-streptomycin for washing the isolated hepatocytes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->
4. Coat the bottom of culture plates or wells by applying 0.01% rat-tail collagen solution. Incubate for 2 hours at room temperature under sterile conditions, then wash the coating with PBS before use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S04 -->

## Procedure

### Surgical Exposure

1. Anesthetize the mouse using isoflurane. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Spray the surgical instruments and the anesthetized mouse with 70% ethanol to sterilize the area. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
3. Once the mouse is nonresponsive, cut open the peritoneal cavity to expose the liver and intestines; ensure not to cut from the diaphragm. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
4. Slide the intestines to the left side of the mouse body to expose the portal vein, and lift the liver lobe sufficiently to expose the vena cava. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->

### Perfusion Step I

1. Set the perfusion pump to deliver Perfusion Solution I at a flow rate of 250 mL/hr. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->
2. Insert the needle into the portal vein. Note that the portal vein is located superior to the inferior vena cava and abdominal aorta, and inferior to the liver's margin. Hold the needle steady without puncturing through the portal vein wall. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S02 -->
3. Quickly turn on the pump and observe the liver swelling slightly to confirm correct needle placement in the portal vein. Immediately cut through the vena cava to relieve pressure and allow outflow. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S03 -->
4. Lay the liver lobes flat and gently massage each lobe by rolling with a wet cotton-tipped swab to evenly distribute Perfusion Solution I. Perfuse approximately 50 mL of the medium at about 500 mL/hr. A successful infusion will cause the liver to blanch and lighten. Periodically massage the liver but avoid overmanipulation to maintain cell viability. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S04 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Ensure the liver lobes never become hard or stiff during Perfusion Step I, as this indicates that an air bubble has passed through the line. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S05 -->

### Perfusion Step II

1. Momentarily turn off the pump, switch the medium line to Perfusion Solution II, and restart the pump at 350 mL/hr. Perfuse 20-40 mL of Perfusion Solution II while periodically massaging the liver. Never allow air to enter the line. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S01 -->
2. Use forceps to squeeze the inferior vena cava for approximately 10 seconds every few minutes during Perfusion Step II. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** If the liver begins to break up before the full volume of digestion medium has been perfused, stop the perfusion immediately and proceed to the next step. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S03 -->

### Harvest and Purification

1. After approximately 40 mL of Perfusion Solution II has perfused through the liver, remove the cannula, excise the liver from the cavity, and place it into a petri dish. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S01 -->
2. Transfer the dish to a sterile hood. Add approximately 20 mL of serum-free DMEM and gently scrape the digested liver with forceps to mechanically break it apart. If the liver does not break apart easily or contains large clumps, the digestion was unsuccessful. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S02 -->
3. Filter the cell mixture through a sterile filter or two layers of sterile gauze into a sterile 50 mL conical tube kept on ice. Adjust the total volume to 50 mL using the DMEM wash medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S03 -->
4. Centrifuge the cells at 1500-1700 rpm for 2 minutes at 4°C. Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 8 mL of cold DMEM. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S04 -->
